## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Varuṇajātaka* (Ja 71) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Canon. In its frame narrative (the "story of the present," *paccuppannavatthu*), set at Jetavana near Sāvatthi, the Buddha delivers the teaching in connection with the Elder Tissa, the Squire's Son. The introductory story recounts how thirty young men of Sāvatthi ordained, completed their initial five-year training under their preceptors, and subsequently requested a meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhāna*) chosen by the Buddha from among thirty-eight meditation themes before departing to embrace the forest-dwelling ascetic life [Shaw 2006]. Modern scholarship notes that this story of the present reflects later commentary-layer developments distinct from the canonical verses [Shaw 2006].
